newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Volatile, thin trade keep Belgian bond buyers away.
newsitem.headline: Volatile, thin trade keep Belgian bond buyers away.

text.p: End investors were in scarce supply in a volatile but thinly traded Belgian linear bond market on Friday, and traders said it looked like staying that way well into next week.
"The most exciting thing next week looks like being the distribution of our bonuses," one trader said.

"There is a fresh auction next week and there are still some end investors with cash to spend," another trader said. "But on the other hand this price volatility coupled with the low volumes is making people nervous about stepping into the market at the moment."
Minutes before the Belgian market closed, EU diplomats said a deal on the stability pact had indeed been struck. No details were immediately available.
The yield of the 2006 OLO was 5.99 percent against Thursday's 6.00, having at one stage been up to 6.07 percent.
The spread over German Bunds was barely changed at 11 basis points against Thursday's closing 10.
The December futures contract was 11 basis points down at 120.44 in a 120.61/120.11 range.
Traders said the Belgian market contented itself with simply tracking other European markets on Friday, with nothing on the horizon to give a solid push in either direction.
The market, which spent the day in negative territory, did pare its loses in the late afternoon.

Traders said confident remarks on the EMU stability pact by Dutch Central Bank President and European Monetary Institute chief designate Wim Duisenberg at the EU summit in Dublin had helped the market.
"Duisenberg saying the stability pact is coming was supportive," one trader said.
